# ethereum-optimism/specs Monthly Report (February 2026)

## 🚀 Highlights
In February 2026, development focused heavily on refining the technical specifications for the Superchain ecosystem, with a particular emphasis on `op-supernode` architecture and interoperability readiness. Significant progress was made in documenting L2 contract upgrade paths and preimage hints for fault proofs, ensuring greater determinism and security. While the team addressed critical synchronization bugs in the supernode's L1 polling mechanism, ongoing technical discussions highlighted the complexities of managing safe labels and Execution Layer (EL) sync behavior across diverse client implementations like Geth and Reth.

## 🛠️ Key Developments

### Protocol & Upgrade Specifications
A major focus this month was formalizing the procedures for network evolution and contract management.
*   **L2 Contract Upgrades:** New specifications were integrated detailing the execution and contract-specific requirements for L2 upgrades, providing a standardized framework for protocol maintenance ([#884](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/pull/884)).
*   **Kona Build Determinism:** Documentation was introduced to define the build determinism invariant for Kona, a critical component for verifiable fault proofs ([#889](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/pull/889)).

### Fault Proofs & Preimage Enhancements
Work continued on the data availability and fault-proof layers to improve the reliability of state transitions.
*   **Preimage Hint Updates:** Documentation for preimage hints was expanded to include `l1-blob` hints and a revised format for `l1-precompile` hints ([#888](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/pull/888)).
*   **Blob Hint Data:** Specifications for blob hint data within the fault-proof documentation were updated to align with current protocol requirements ([#890](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/pull/890)).

### Infrastructure & Tooling
*   **Flashblocks Support:** Technical discussions explored integrating `Flashblocks` support into `op-geth`, leveraging existing work from the Firehose Live Tracer to improve block production speeds and user experience ([#756](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/issues/756)).

## 🐛 Issues & Triage

### Closed Issues
*   **Supernode L1 Polling:** A critical bug was resolved where `op-supernode` instances using HTTP L1 RPC URLs would inadvertently disable L1 polling, causing virtual nodes to fall behind on L1 head updates ([#19012](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/issues/19012)).

### New & Active Issues
*   **`op-supernode` Label Management:** Extensive discussion is underway regarding how the Consensus Layer (CL) and Execution Layer (EL) safe labels are controlled. The current direction suggests the CL should remain the primary controller of the engine while the supernode directly manages EL safe/finalized states to prevent synchronization conflicts ([#18976](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/issues/18976)).
*   **Initial EL Sync UX:** Developers are investigating a bug where the `op-node` may incorrectly mark blocks as finalized during the initial sync process. This includes exploring how Snap Sync should follow the finalized L2 tip as a maximum target ([#17631](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/issues/17631)).
*   **Interop Readiness:** The `TestInteropReadiness` acceptance test remains a blocker for interop proofs, requiring the super DG to support explicit output roots before it can be unskipped ([#18616](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/issues/18616)).
*   **Data Availability Inconsistencies:** Inconsistencies in naming conventions and symlinks for `op-reth` snapshots on `datadirs.optimism.io` were identified, potentially affecting node operators' ability to sync archival data ([#536](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/issues/536)).

## 💬 Community & Collaboration
The month was characterized by deep technical coordination between core contributors regarding the "Supernode" architecture. Notable collaboration occurred between contributors like `geoknee` and `axelKingsley` on defining stateful controller boundaries, and `maoueh` and `sunjiahui` on the potential migration of Flashblock support into the main `op-geth` codebase. There is also active troubleshooting involving the developer experience, specifically addressing `BlockNotFoundError` issues in the withdrawal flow by comparing the Optimism SDK's validation logic against Viem's implementation ([#1956](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/specs/issues/1956)).
